\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Contraction}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Randomization.Contraction
\section{Overview}
Coordinate noise admits a negative contraction rate depending only on its exponent. Positive and negative coordinate contractions combine into contraction for anisotropic noise with independent signs.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Negative coordinate noise contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinate_noise_negative_contraction}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.CenteredContraction.scalar_contraction, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.condExp_negative_moment_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinateNoise}
\difficulty{4}
For every $q\ge2$ there exists $0<c\le1$, with $c=2/5$ if $q=4$, such that for every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, every coordinate $i$, and every real function $f$ on its outcome space, $\|N_{i,-c}f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{q,P}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $N_{i,a}h=E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h+a(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Self-adjoint coordinate noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinateNoise_selfAdjoint}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_selfAdjoint, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinateNoise}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, a coordinate $i$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\mathbb E_P[(N_{i,\rho}f)g]=\mathbb E_P[fN_{i,\rho}g]$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $N_{i,a}h=E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h+a(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Partial anisotropic noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.partialNoise}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $J\subseteq[n]$, rates $r_i\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Define $T_{J,\boldsymbol r}f(x)=\sum_S(\prod_{j\in S\cap J}r_j)f_S(x)$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components).
\end{definition}

\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.partialNoise_insert}

For $T_{J,\boldsymbol r}f=\sum_S(\prod_{j\in S\cap J}r_j)f_S$, $T_{J\cup\{i\},\boldsymbol r}f=N_{i,r_i}(T_{J,\boldsymbol r}f)$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $N_{i,a}h=E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h+a(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Anisotropic contraction from coordinate bounds]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.anisotropicNoise_norm_le_of_coordinate}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.component_reconstruction, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.anisotropicNoise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinateNoise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.partialNoise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.partialNoise_insert}

Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $q\in\mathbb R$, and rates $r_i\in\mathbb R$. If $\|N_{i,r_i}g\|_{q,P}\le\|g\|_{q,P}$ for every coordinate $i$ and every real $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, then $\|T_{\boldsymbol r}f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{q,P}$ for every real $f$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_{\boldsymbol s}h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}(\prod_{i\in S}s_i)h_S$ for real coordinate rates $s_i$; $N_{i,a}h=E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h+a(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)$; $\|h\|_{q,P}:=(\mathbb E_P|h|^q)^{1/q}$ as a totalized moment expression for every real $q$, with $1/0=0$, $0^0=1$, and $0^b=0$ for $b\ne0$.
\end{theorem}
